cards.title: 12.1 The Eritrean Constitution
body: On 14 December, 1950, the UN General Assembly elected a Bolivian diplomat, Eduardo Anze Matienzo to become a UN Commissioner in Eritrea.
Soon thereafter, he started to prepare a draft constitution in consultation with Eritrean notables and representatives of political parties.

cards.title: The federal arrangement
body: Under the UN arrangement Eritrea had its own **constitution** (adopted in 1952), an elected **Assembly**, a Chief Executive, its own flag and official languages (Tigrinya and Arabi

cards.title: 12.2 The Eritrean Government between 1952 and 1955
body: Accordingly, it had the mandate of only ratifying the Eritrean constitution and had to dissolve after it completed its job.
Tedla Bairu was confirmed as the chief executive of the Eritrean government, and Ali Radai was continued to chair the National Assembly.

lessons.title: Ethiopia’s Gradual Abrogation of the Federation and Eritreans Reaction

cards.title: 12.3 Ethiopia’s Gradual Abrogation of the Federation and Eritreans Reaction
body: According to the provisions of the Federal Act, a Federal Council was supposed to be formed with equal number of Ethiopian and Eritrean representatives.
The task of the Federal Council was to advice Emperor Haileselasie on common matters of the Federation such as defense, foreign affairs, and currency.

cards.title: Gradual abrogation of the federation
body: The Ethiopian government steadily undermined Eritrean autonomy: political parties and the free press were suppressed, Amharic replaced Tigrinya and Arabic as the official language,
